rationale: Keep Sunrise Renewables as one staffed U.S. solar and battery-development platform, but correct its ownership from CI IV to the directly filed CI V chain. Remove the unsupported green-hydrogen scope, Kentucky-headquarters claim and 2022 investment-date inference. Treat Lost City and the disclosed South Carolina projects as underlying developments, not separate manager-level PortCos.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Sunrise Renewables is a staffed Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners development platform for utility-scale solar and battery-storage projects in the United States. Kentucky regulatory filings identify the legal vehicle as CI V Sunrise Renewables LLC, held through CI V Sunrise HoldCo LLC, and place the Lost City project SPV beneath that chain. The filings also identify Sunrise personnel working across Lost City Solar in Kentucky and disclosed solar and battery developments in South Carolina. Sunrise is therefore retained as the manager-level CI V platform, while Lost City, Gullah Geechee Renewable Energy Center Solar, Cypress Gardens BESS and their SPVs remain underlying projects. Public evidence does not support the prior CI IV ownership, a green-hydrogen scope, a Kentucky headquarters or a 2022 CIP entry date. A New York business address appears in filings, but the formal headquarters is not publicly disclosed. No operating project, platform sale, ownership transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.
